messages:
Maya Patel: @oncall-bot paging: GPU OOM spike on prefill path, multiple container restarts in us-west-2 cluster A. impact: some requests returning 500s. Logs show CUDA OOM during large prefill. /cc @Kevin

Oncall Bot: :rotating_light: Pager received by Maya Patel, severity P1. Runbook: start triage, notify SRE, attach logs. incident_id=inc-1865

Maya Patel: Observed ~30 restarts across pool gpu-a-9 over the last 12m, restart loop on models/llama-4x-lg-quant. Requests contained very long context windows (~650k tokens) from customer 'synth' hitting route /generate/v1.

Kevin Liu: seeing identical traces: `cudaMalloc failed: out of memory` in prefill stage. container log excerpt:
``
2026-03-15T10:05:12Z ERROR runtime: prefill failed: allocation 268435456 bytes: CUDA OOM
stack: serve/runtime/prefill.go:172
```

Jordan Kim: Paging oncall-sre. Probable contributors: unbounded long prompts on customer side, KV cache blowup during prefill, and a recent kernel-driver rollout on a subset of nodes. Also quantization kernels sometimes change allocator behavior.

Tanisha Gomez: Customer success: we have 12 active customers on that pool; early ticket from 'synth' flagged spikes and errors. If impact widens we need a public status update.

Kevin Liu: Quick mitigations in flight:
- disable prefill for very long-window routes (route-level trimming) -> `redwood route update`
- map noisy callers to a smaller/fallback model to avoid GPU prefill
- reduce KV cache retention (lower eviction threshold)

Deploy Bot: Triggered change: `PATCH /pools/gpu-a-9/eviction` -> scaleRetention=0.25

Maya Patel: Applying route filter to drop >200k token prefill requests. Command executed:
``
# temporary rule to prevent huge prefills
redwood route update --id r_1234 --prefill-max-tokens 200000
```

SRE Bot: Oncall Jordan Kim taking lead. Suggest pinning currently restarting instances to coldmodel fallback to break restart loop.

Jordan Kim: Doing node-level mitigation now: cordoning node gpu-a-9-7, draining pods, restarting NVIDIA driver on remaining nodes, and rolling runtime with `--prefill-trim` flag. Also enabling route->fallback map for the noisy callers.

Maya Patel: After route filter and fallback mapping, restarts reduced from ~1/min to ~1 every 8-10 min. CPU fallback reduced throughput but prevented OOM-driven crashes. Error rate down ~73%.

Kevin Liu: Open question: why runtime didn't fall back before killing container? Looks like allocator path for quantized kernels doesn't check prefill peak in some codepaths. Opening PR for extra guard: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4521

Tanisha Gomez: Draft customer update:
"We're actively mitigating a GPU memory issue impacting large-context requests in us-west-2. We've applied temporary routing and fallbacks; some requests may see higher latency. We're monitoring closely and will follow up with the root cause and timeline."

Maya Patel: Agreed. Posting to status page now.

Deploy Bot: Status page: `INC-1865` created, incident page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-1865

Jordan Kim: Next steps: reproduce with a controlled long-prefill test in staging (script attached in ticket), audit prefill allocator path, add runtime OOM-safe fallback to map to coldmodel before container kill, and improve telemetry for peak prefill allocations.

Maya Patel: Adding temporary alert: `prefill_restart_rate > 5/min` -> page oncall. Rule created.

Kevin Liu: Scheduling maintenance window to roll driver on us-west-2 nodes tomorrow 02:00 UTC to ensure uniform driver/kernel state.

Customer Success: synth: acknowledged; asking for ETA on restored performance. I'll send hourly updates.

Maya Patel: Closing live mitigation loop — moving to RCA and post-incident analysis. Incident remains open for follow-up.

SRE Bot: :white_check_mark: Handoff note: oncall -> Jordan Kim for RCA, Maya Patel for customer comms, Kevin Liu for runtime fix. participants: Jordan Kim, Maya Patel, Kevin Liu, Tanisha Gomez
